details.summary: A superb, practical recipe that perfectly balances the dietary needs for MASLD and type 2 diabetes in a flavorful 20-minute skillet meal. Only a minor fix is needed to add the unlisted black pepper to the ingredient list.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is highly coherent. Cumin, oregano, garlic, and lime paired with pork, black beans, and rice is a classic, foolproof Cuban-inspired combination.
Step 1 calls for 'a pinch of black pepper,' but black pepper is not included in the ingredient list. Add it to the list to ensure complete consistency.
Instructions are excellent. They provide proper time ranges (4 to 6 minutes), visual cues (browned and cooked through, softened), check instructions at minimum times, and a halfway flip for the pork.
The ingredients and techniques align perfectly with a weeknight Cuban-American style, heavily featuring the characteristic mojo profile of citrus and earthy spices.
Pan-searing thin medallions is the ideal way to cook lean pork tenderloin quickly without drying it out. Sautéing the vegetables and warming the beans/rice in the same skillet works perfectly.
The computed nutrition values align seamlessly with the specified quantities of pork, brown rice, black beans, and olive oil.

The title accurately reflects the dish. The intro highlights the main ingredients and focuses on practical, sensible benefits ('steady-digesting carbohydrate', 'energy stable') without using banned health claims.
This is a highly appetizing, colorful, and practical weeknight dinner. It transforms simple staples into an exciting meal.

Brilliantly serves both conditions. It provides the high-quality, high-fiber carbohydrates (brown rice, black beans) needed for stable blood sugar, alongside the lean protein, vegetables, and olive oil required for a liver-friendly profile.
Zero added sugar, and it hits the carbohydrate window perfectly (42.9 g) using excellent quality sources (whole grain rice and legumes).

Fits perfectly into the lean meat dinners chapter. It is a true one-pan skillet meal featuring a measured portion of lean pork, whole grains, and a bright pan sauce built from lime juice rather than cream or butter.
Easily achievable in under 30 minutes from a cold start. The smart use of ready-to-eat cooked brown rice and quick-cooking pork medallions respects the cook's time while using everyday ingredients.
